findings.rationale: rewrite_lvalue ignores the bound set, mis-qualifying shadowed state names. rewrite_expr guards Expr::Var with `!bound.contains(&name)` before prefixing (lines 711-717), but rewrite_lvalue (687-698) threads `bound` into the recursion yet rewrite_state_name (700-706) never consults it. Trigger: inside a ForAll whose binder name shadows a component state name, an lvalue (LValue::Var or LValue::Index) on that name is prefixed to `alias.<name>` on the assignment target while the same name in an expression stays unqualified, producing inconsistent/corrupted rewrites (e.g. `x[i] = x` where `x` is the binder). The presence of `bound` as a parameter to rewrite_lvalue suggests the check was intended but dropped.

sync_action uses unreachable!() which can abort instead of returning CoreError. At lines 1051-1058, sync_action pattern-matches rewrite_component_item's result on SpecItem::Action with an `else { unreachable!() }`. The input is selected as an Action (line 1034), so this is safe only if rewrite_component_item preserves the Action variant — a behavior outside this projection. If it ever maps an Action to a non-Action, the process panics/aborts, violating the documented contract that lower_compose returns CoreError for invalid inputs rather than aborting.

init metadata uses first-wins, silently discarding later components' init meta. init_meta is set only while `init_meta.is_none()` (lines 320-322 for component inits, 346-348 for compose-level inits). When several components each declare init metadata, only the first component's meta survives in the merged SpecItem::Init (360-364); later meta is silently dropped without error or warning, which can lose per-component init provenance in the composed kernel.
